newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called up $4, Brent flat to 5cts down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called up $4, Brent flat to 5cts down.

text.p: The IPE August gas oil contract was expected to open some four dollars a tonne up on Tuesday to catch up with a late rally on crude and U.S. products market, brokers said.
IPE September Brent crude oil was called steady to five cents below Monday's $19.46 a barrel settle.

The contract gained some 50 cents on Monday as traders came in to cover short positions following news that the U.N. had approved the Iraqi aid distribution plan, paving the way for resumed crude exports.
Surging U.S. gasoline prices also helped futures market gains. High demand has tightened supply of reformulated gasoline and unscheduled refinery outages have curbed supplies of the product.
Markets also rose when Occidental shut its 175,000 bpd Cano Limon field in Colombia and declared force majeure on loadings following rebel attacks on the pipeline.
But the focus is now back on Iraq and the upcoming weekly U.S stock statistics from the American Petroleum Institute.
"The key now is how much Iraq is going to export, and tonight's API's," one said, adding that following the large draw in last week's U.S API gasoline stocks, few traders would short the market.
U.S. gasoline stocks to the week ending 25 July were down over three million barrels. Some traders expected a further draw in this weeks report, brokers said.
